qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant acute-care hospital networks and ambulatory surgery centers with 30-50% bed share in high-growth Sunbelt MSAs create irreplaceable physical healthcare infrastructure with Certificate of Need and capital barriers. Empirical proof shown by 10-year median ROIC of 24.9% and industry-leading ~19-20% EBITDA margins. Local market density enables mid-single-digit (4-5%) annual commercial rate increases that offset wage inflation, though government payer rate pressures (Medicare/Medicaid) present ongoing margin constraints.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Premier US hospital operator with unmatched Sunbelt density and Frist family stewardship, but capital structure is burdened by $41.6B in long-term debt (6.13x LT debt/net income vs 4.0x ceiling) and negative equity (-$6.0B) resulting from multi-year debt-funded share repurchases. [5-10Y g: organic admissions 2.5% + commercial pricing/acuity mix 2.5% + margin 0.0% + net buybacks 2.5%]
qualitative.evidence: SEC EDGAR data confirms 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 24.9% (20.6% in FY2016 to 27.9% in FY2025) and FCF conversion of 107% in FY2025 ($8.7B Owner FCF vs $6.8B NI). However, long-term debt stands at $41,603M against $1,040M cash (Net Debt $40.6B) and FY2025 net income of $6,784M, yielding a 6.13x LT debt / NI ratio (far exceeding the 4.0x maximum). Stockholders' equity is -$6,027M due to aggressive debt-funded buybacks over the decade, triggering the disqualifying financial engineering red flag. Operating interest coverage has averaged 4.0x-5.4x across the cycle, falling short of the >5.0x through-the-cycle peace-of-mind fortress standard.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
